confidence: Low; everyone has motive, but culpability still requires access and delivery evidence.
plausibility_notes: Artie's accepted job is a welcome complication that reduces an initially obvious motive.

The 30 speeches have a conspicuously repeated pattern: I concealed or compromised something; Grant discovered it and threatened exposure or demanded more. Individually coherent, collectively formulaic.
Grant's simultaneous blackmail of nearly everyone strains human plausibility more than the individual secrets do.
Three people append precise first-entry times to motive speeches. Those statements sound planted to serve future timeline elimination rather than naturally arising in a motive discussion.
No truth guarantee means these remain claims; late-entry assertions cannot yet eliminate suspects.
Minnie admitting an undisclosed blackout is a meaningful risky confession; candid confession by so many people feels like game procedure rather than ordinary self-protection.
